text: Four chapters in, and you haven't written a single formula. That's about to change — and here's exactly why it matters.

DAX — Data Analysis Expressions — is the formula language behind every calculation in Power BI. Here's the simplest one possible: a measure that sums a column. On its own, that's nothing a dragged field couldn't do. The payoff comes once this measure has a name — you can reuse it inside other formulas instead of repeating the same SUM everywhere.

Here's what a real DAX formula unlocks: comparing this quarter's sales against last quarter's. That's not something a dragged field can produce — it took one formula, filtering the same column down to a different period. That's the gap DAX fills, and it's what the rest of this chapter is about.
Next: the anatomy of a DAX formula — every piece, in plain language.
